title: EU AI Act — System Classification Questionnaire
description: Guided questionnaire used by the deterministic classifier. Answers plus the rule-set version fully determine the risk tier — no model is involved in tiering.
legal_notice: This tool provides compliance tooling, not legal advice.

questions.prompt: Is the system placed on the EU market, put into service in the EU, or is its output used within the EU?
questions.help: The EU AI Act applies based on an EU nexus. This is recorded for applicability context; it does not change the risk tier.

questions.prompt: Does the system evaluate or classify people over time based on social behaviour or personal characteristics, leading to detrimental or unjustified treatment?
questions.help: General-purpose social scoring of natural persons by public or private actors.

questions.prompt: Does the system perform real-time remote biometric identification of people in publicly accessible spaces for law-enforcement purposes?
questions.help: Narrow law-enforcement exemptions exist but are out of scope for self-classification here.

questions.prompt: Does the system infer the emotions of individuals in the workplace or in education settings?
questions.help: Except where used strictly for medical or safety reasons.

questions.prompt: Does the system categorise people using biometric data to infer sensitive attributes (race, political opinions, trade-union membership, religion, sex life, sexual orientation)?
questions.help: Excludes lawful labelling/filtering in the law-enforcement context.

questions.prompt: Does the system assess or predict the risk of a person committing a criminal offence based solely on profiling or personality traits?
questions.help: Does not cover systems supporting human assessment based on objective, verifiable facts linked to criminal activity.

questions.prompt: Does the system create or expand facial-recognition databases through untargeted scraping of images from the internet or CCTV?
Is the AI a safety component of a product — or itself a product — covered by EU harmonisation legislation (Annex I) that requires third-party conformity assessment?
questions.help: E.g. machinery, medical devices, toys, lifts. Triggers high-risk under Art. 6(1).

questions.prompt: Which Annex III high-risk use category best describes the system's intended purpose?

options.label: Safety of critical infrastructure (water, gas, electricity, traffic)
Employment / HR (recruitment, screening, task allocation, evaluation)
Access to essential private/public services (credit scoring, benefits, insurance pricing)

questions.help: Select the closest category. 'None' if the system's purpose is not listed in Annex III.

questions.prompt: If an Annex III category was selected: does the system perform only a narrow procedural task, improve the result of a prior human activity, detect decision-making patterns without replacing human judgement, or perform a purely preparatory task — AND not profile people or materially influence decisions?
questions.help: This is the Art. 6(3) derogation. If ALL conditions hold, an otherwise-Annex-III system is NOT high-risk. Leave false if unsure.

questions.prompt: Does the system directly interact with natural persons (e.g. a chatbot or virtual assistant)?
questions.help: Triggers a transparency obligation to inform people they are interacting with an AI system.

questions.prompt: Does the system generate or manipulate image, audio, video, or text content (including deepfakes or generative AI output)?
questions.help: Triggers a transparency obligation to mark/disclose AI-generated or manipulated content.
